rows: GENERAL NOTES COVERING BILL OF QUANTITIES
These notes shall apply to all Bills of Quantities forming part of this document.
The Works under this Bill shall be priced based on re-measurable quantities unless otherwise mentioned.

This Bill shall be read in conjunction with the Drawings, Specifications of Materials and Workmanship, General Conditions of Contract, and all other associated Bills of Quantities. All these documents shall be construed as being complementary to one another, and any requirement shown on one shall be binding as though it appeared on all.

The Contractor shall provide and execute everything reasonably necessary for the proper completion of the Works according to the true intent and meaning of the Drawings, Specifications, and Contract Documents, whether or not the same is specifically mentioned, provided that it can be reasonably inferred therefrom.

In the event of any discrepancy between the Drawings, Specifications, or any other Contract Documents, the same shall be immediately brought to the notice of the Employer’s Representative / Consultant, whose decision shall be final and binding.

Tenderers shall carefully examine all drawings, specifications, site conditions, and existing services before submitting their bid, and shall satisfy themselves as to the nature and scope of the works to be carried out. No claim shall be entertained on account of lack of knowledge of site conditions.
Unit rates shall be inclusive of all mock-ups, samples, protection, cleaning, rectification, and housekeeping till handover.

Quoted rate shall include all charges towards transportation, lead, lift, mathadi charges , Octroi, installation, levies, royalties, WCP & CAR insurance & other applicable insurances, ESI & PF premiums, overheards, fees and rectification of defects or replacement of defective material.
Scope of Work and Pricing Requirements
The rates and prices quoted shall be deemed to include the entire scope of work as defined in the Drawings, Specifications, and BOQ.

The quoted unit rates shall be comprehensive and shall include the cost of all labour, materials, plants, tools, tackles, equipment, transportation, loading, unloading, wastage, scaffolding, staging, overheads, profits, and all incidental expenses necessary for the proper execution and completion of the works.

The Contractor shall make necessary provisions in the rates for all contingencies, difficulties, or unforeseen circumstances that may arise during the execution of the works, ensuring the satisfactory completion of the project.

For the valuation of variations, any addition or omission to the Contract Sum shall be based on the measured quantities applying the relevant unit rates (or pro-rated unit rate, as the case may be) contained in the BOQ. Contractors are therefore advised to quote each item in a fair, realistic, and complete manner.

Unless otherwise specifically stated, the tendered rates shall be inclusive of all duties, levies, royalties, insurance, freight, loading, unloading, storage, protection, wastages, and safety provisions at site.

The rates quoted shall also include all costs for preparing and presenting mock-ups, providing samples and prototypes for approval prior to mass procurement, and obtaining written approval from the Client / Consultant.
Items Deemed to be Included in the Quoted Rates
Unless specifically stated otherwise, the quoted rates for each item shall be deemed to include but not be limited to the following:
a) Supply of all materials, fittings, fixtures, and accessories required for execution, including transportation to site, unloading, safe storage, handling, and protection till completion.
b) All necessary labour, supervision, skilled and unskilled manpower, and tools required for satisfactory execution of work at all heights, levels, and confined spaces.

c) Providing and subsequently removing all scaffolding, staging, platforms, ladders, safety barricades, and other temporary works required for execution, including double height areas, partitions, and false ceilings.
d) Hiring, operating, and maintaining all tools, plants, and machinery necessary for execution as per the specifications.
e) Receiving, unloading, storing, protecting, and handling all materials supplied either by the Employer or the Contractor, including all ancillary works required for fixing in position.

f) All costs associated with assembling, setting out, fitting, and fixing materials in position, including making necessary adjustments and allowances for overlaps, laps, jointing, and cutting wastage.
g) All necessary protection of executed works from damage and making good of any disturbed works.
h) Removal of all debris, waste, and surplus materials from the site on a regular basis and after completion of the works in compliance with site housekeeping norms.
i) All incidental works necessary for proper completion of the works, including minor items not specifically mentioned but reasonably implied.
j) All establishment charges, overheads, profits, and statutory compliance costs.

The Contractor shall visit the site before submission of tender and satisfy himself regarding the access, working space, site constraints, service routes, and other conditions likely to affect the execution of the works.
The Contractor shall verify all levels, dimensions, and conditions shown in the drawings and shall be responsible for the accuracy of the same before commencement of work.
The Contractor shall co-ordinate with all other contractors and agencies working at site for proper sequencing of work to avoid delays and conflicts.
Temporary storage of materials shall be arranged by the Contractor in areas approved by the Employer / PMC, ensuring that materials are stacked safely and without obstructing other works.
The Contractor shall arrange necessary labour, tools, and equipment for hoisting materials to upper floors and transporting debris down from elevated levels.
The Contractor shall protect existing finishes, structures, and services from damage during execution and shall make good any damage caused at his cost.
All necessary safety precautions and site-specific protection shall be maintained throughout the execution of works.
The Contractor shall prepare and submit detailed shop drawings for all works and obtain approval from the Employer’s Representative / Consultant prior to commencement.

For all custom-made or modular furniture, the Contractor shall submit 3D rendered indicative images, detailing the design intent, finishes, and joinery construction at the time of technical bid evaluation.
Specialized and proprietary system works shall be executed strictly as per manufacturer’s specifications, standards, and installation manuals.
All makes, models, and finishes of materials shall be submitted for approval and shall not be procured or installed without written confirmation from the Employer / Consultant.
All paints, polishes, and finishes shall be LEED-compliant and conform to VOC emission standards applicable to LEED Commercial Interiors.
All proprietary system items shall be installed by authorized dealers or certified applicators, and necessary certificates shall be produced for verification.
The Contractor shall ensure adherence to quality standards for workmanship, alignment, finish, and performance as defined in the project specifications.
Quantities shall be measured in accordance with IS: 1200 – Method of Measurement of Building and Civil Engineering Works, unless otherwise specified.
All work shall be measured net as fixed in position.
Partitions shall be measured from finished floor level to the underside of true ceiling, unless stated otherwise.
Column cladding areas shall be measured from finished floor to false ceiling.
Counters shall be measured on visible plan area or length, and cabinetry shall be measured from visible front elevation only.
The measurement for blinds shall be based on visible elevation area only.
For hard flooring areas (granite, marble, vitrified, etc.), payment shall be made only for the visible laid area. No extra payment shall be made for cutting, wastage, or trimming.
All wastages shall be deemed to be included in the quoted unit rates.
No additional claim shall be entertained for variations arising due to site conditions, minor adjustments, or coordination with other trades.
The Contractor shall execute all works in a neat, workmanlike, and safe manner in compliance with local regulations and building codes.
All works shall be properly sequenced with other services to ensure smooth execution and commissioning.
The Contractor shall clear debris and waste material from the site on a daily basis to maintain cleanliness.
All common areas, builder lobbies, and access routes used by the Contractor shall be cleaned and restored to original condition upon completion.
Floors shall be scrapped, cleaned, and wet-mopped before final floor finishes such as carpets are laid.
Water and power required for execution shall be provided free of cost. However, any wastage will attract a penalty at the sole discretion of Client.
Necessary permits, gate passes, and clearances for material movement shall be arranged by the Contractor in coordination with the site management.
Commercial grade plywood shall be used in all joinery unless otherwise approved in writing by the PMC / Architect.
All furniture, storage, and tables shall be factory-finished unless specific site finishing is approved.
All gaps between slabs, glazing, columns, walls, and false floors shall be properly filled and sealed to maintain visual and acoustic integrity.
Touch-up and finishing of all existing doors and elements handed over by the builder shall form part of the Contractor’s scope.
Countertop rates shall include necessary cutouts for sinks, basins, taps, and polishing of exposed edges to the satisfaction of the Architect.
All mild steel sections shall be painted with one coat of metal primer and two coats of enamel paint unless otherwise stated.
The Contractor shall ensure that all materials used are of approved make, new, free from defects, and conforming to the specifications.
All “Rate Only (R/O)”/ QRO (Quote Rate only) items shall be quoted without exception; unquoted items shall render the bid invalid.
The rates quoted under R/O items are negotiable, and only rationalized rates shall be considered during execution.
Basic rates of materials shall exclude taxes, transportation, wastages, leads, and lifts; all such costs shall be included in the quoted rate.
Taxes shall be extra as applicable at the time of billing.
The Contractor shall not be entitled to any escalation of rates during the tenure of the contract.
Any additional items required to complete the works as per scope, drawings, or specifications shall be executed without claiming extra cost unless approved in writing.
The decision of the Employer / Project Manager / Consultant shall be final and binding in all matters relating to interpretation of the BOQ, specifications, and scope.
Contractor must maintain and regularly update material spreadsheets throughout construction for LEED documentation.
Track and document all applicable credits: construction & demolition waste, recycled content, regional materials, rapidly renewable materials, certified wood, low-emitting materials, etc.
Collect and file all material documentation from subcontractors and suppliers.
Schedule a mid-project audit with the LEED consultant to verify completeness of documentation.
Take and archive photographs (site work, materials, waste handling) to support LEED submission and demonstrate sustainable practices.
Contractor must ensure full compliance with the Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, including obtaining/maintaining valid labour licence, registers, wage records, and statutory submissions.
Contractor is responsible for ensuring all subcontracted labour is legally engaged, paid as per law, and covered under applicable statutory benefits (ESI, PF, WC insurance etc.).
The Contractor shall comply with all applicable laws, local regulations, labour laws, and statutory requirements during execution.
Adequate safety measures shall be implemented, including PPE usage, barricading, and fire safety equipment.
Proper signage shall be displayed for restricted zones and safety instructions.
Work shall be carried out with due care to prevent damage to adjoining properties, services, and structures.
All works shall conform to relevant Indian Standards and local building codes in force at the time of execution.

Providing of Waterproofing - Chemical Treatment with Primer: The slab shall be thoroughly cleaned of all dirt, dust, and grit. Apply a suitable primer over the clean surface as per manufacturer’s instructions, followed by 3 coats of chemical waterproofing treatment on the floor. Apply a base coat of 1:6 cement-sand mortar over the treated surface on the floor and on peripheral walls up to 450 mm. The cost shall include surface cleaning, primer, chemical treatment, and base coat application. The waterproofed area shall be ponded and tested for a minimum of 24 hours or as per manufacturer’s specifications. Warranty: Up to 10 years.

* Clean surface to remove all dust, foreign matters, loose particles or any deposits of contaminants which could affect the bond between the surface and waterproof coating.
* Remove all sharp projections and make surface reasonably smooth
* Thoroughly pre-wet all concrete surfaces for at least one hour prior to application of coating, by ponding of water on flat surfaces and by vigorous spraying of water on vertical surfaces.
* Remove all water from surfaces prior to applying of water proof coating, so that the surface is only damp or surface dry. Standing water or shiny wet surface shall not be present under any circumstances
* Apply water proof coating / Brush Topping as specified for various conditions.
* Apply 12mm thick cement plaster 1:4 (1cement : 4 coarse sand) after applications of final coat.
* After application of final coat of Tape Crete, allow to air dry for 4-6 hours. Do not use any water for curing during this time.
* In case of high temperatures and low humidity combined with high wind condition, cover the coating with polythene sheet to prevent rapid drying.
* Maximum 6 hours after final application, moist cure for 24 hours by spraying water. Ensure that at no time during this 24 hour period the coating is completely dry or completely submerged in water.
* After moist curing, allow to air dry for 3 days.
* After air drying, complete the curing by submersion in water for 24 hours.
